method: 24h volume of pools pairing the token with its redemption unit or a priced quote (ETH/WETH/stETH/wstETH/rETH/weETH for ETH tokens, WBTC/cbBTC for BTC wrappers); mechanics verified in Etherscan-verified source and eth_call at block 26,161,812 unless the row says docs

not_ranked.stETH, wstETH, weETH, rsETH, ezETH, rETH: already in the book or priced by the 2026-10-09 study
not_ranked.WBTC, cbBTC, cirBTC, kBTC, SolvBTC: custodial wrappers redeemable only by merchants or account holders (permissioned)

rows.redemption: redeemForBtc to a bitcoin script (redeem before 2025-11-20); flat 10,000-sat fee; NAV 1/oracle ratio, 1.00485 BTC on 2026-10-09
rows.access: permissionless redemption to any bitcoin script; BTC paid off chain by Lombard, at LBTC x getRate (48 of 55 sampled payouts matched on Bitcoin); the bid's return leg (BTC -> cbBTC 1:1) needs a Coinbase account
rows.queue: measured on Bitcoin for a sample: request to payout median 5.4 days (2026-09, 20 payouts) and 6.0 days (2025, 28 payouts), max 10.2; Lombard docs say 7-9 days; the simulation uses 9
rows.verdict: PROPOSED (lombard-lbtc-queue-bid): cbBTC pools only, $10M, $111,136 a year out of sample (CI $65,117 to $165,420); all five pools give $109,761 at $10M but mix in WBTC's basis

rows.redemption: OETH vault requestWithdrawal -> claimWithdrawal, WETH 1:1, no fee
rows.access: permissionless; only the requester can claim
rows.verdict: too small: $6,141 a year out of sample at $3M (CI $1,861 to $11,344); the queue pays in minutes (median 20 minutes, p90 4.9 days) and the issuer's ARM bids too; payouts exact (693 claims)

rows.redemption: TBTCVault.unmintAndRedeem -> Bridge redemption; 0.2% treasury fee + bitcoin tx fee (<= 100,000 sats)
rows.queue: median 4.9h request to completion proof (1,000 requests, 2025-09/11)
rows.verdict: not proposed: $58,834 a year out of sample at $30M but the interval starts at $1,840, October 2025's crash carries it and the trailing 90 days run at $1,787; 21bp fee; WBTC quotes carry their own basis

rows.redemption: swEXIT createWithdrawRequest (max 500 swETH) -> finalizeWithdrawal; pays amount x min(rate at request, processed rate)
rows.queue: not measured; 47 requests unprocessed at the 2026-10-10 read
rows.verdict: too thin: one Uniswap v3 5bp pool with $0.16M reserve carries the volume

rows.redemption: EthOsTokenRedeemer enterExitQueue -> claimExitedAssets at NAV when processed (accrues while queued)
rows.access: permissioned until 2026-09-03 (redeemer was a Safe); open since
rows.queue: ~11h median since 2026-09-16; 29.23 osETH unprocessed since 2026-09-30; funding needs a privileged positions manager
rows.verdict: permissioned for 23 of the 24 months; too new to price, watch

rows.redemption: FraxEtherRedemptionQueue v1: enterRedemptionQueue -> burnRedemptionTicketNft after a fixed maturity; fee 0 since 2023-11
rows.queue: fixed maturity 30 days now (7 to 60 days since 2023); claims can revert while the contract is underfunded (1,167 ETH vs 1,300 ETH owed)
rows.verdict: too small: $0.12M a day against a 30-day lock worth ~22bp of staking carry

rows.redemption: ERC-4626 to frxETH, then the frxETH queue
rows.verdict: too small ($0.05M a day, through a three-coin pool)

rows.redemption: Mantle Staking unstakeRequest -> claimUnstakeRequest; ETH fixed at request; no fee
rows.verdict: too small on Ethereum ($0.03M a day; mETH liquidity lives on Mantle)

rows.redemption: PufferVault ERC-4626 redeem/withdraw, instant, 1% exit fee, capped by vault ETH (287 ETH)
rows.verdict: too small ($0.03M a day); the 1% instant exit caps the discount
